lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, The case is closed! Great detective work! Today, we walk out of the cave and follow the echoes. Look! There's an old theater in the hills. It's called the Theater of Echoes. An old owl stands at the door. His name is Mr. Hoot. He says, Welcome to the theater! The show starts soon. Say it with me. Welcome to the theater! The show starts soon. Great! Listen. Can you hear the echo? Soon, soon, soon. It's very quiet. Let's read the old sign on the theater door. "Theater of Echoes. Shows every Saturday night. Actors and singers are welcome. Please speak with feeling. When a play is full of real feeling, our echoes will come back. From Mr. Hoot, the director." Who is the director? Mr. Hoot is. What brings the echoes back? Real feeling. Now, phonics. Today, we use our voice with feeling. Really?! High and excited. Oh, really… Low and quiet. Okay! High and happy. Well, okay… Low and slow. Your voice can show your feelings. Let's find our seats!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Welcome to the theater! The show starts soon. Today, we meet the actors at the theater. Mr. Hoot has a small group of actors. One of them is Lulu, a rabbit. She loves the stage. She says, I enjoy dancing. After enjoy, we use an ing word. I enjoy acting. I enjoy singing. Then, ask your friend, How about you? Say it with me. I enjoy acting. How about you? Wonderful! Let's read the actors' board in the hall. "Meet our actors! Lulu the rabbit enjoys dancing and jumping. Mr. Hoot enjoys reading old plays. Echo, the voice of the theater, enjoys repeating your words. We need new actors for our next play. Do you enjoy acting? Come and join us!" What does Lulu enjoy? Dancing and jumping. What does Echo enjoy? Repeating your words. Now, phonics. Let's use our voice again. Yes! I got it! High and happy. Yes… I think so. Low and quiet. Thank you so much! Bright and excited. Thank you… goodbye. Soft and a little sad. Great feelings! Now, tell me, what do you enjoy?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I enjoy acting. How about you? Today, Mr. Hoot shows us his old play. It's called The Princess and the Dragon. The play needs actors. Which role do you want? Haru wants a big role. He says, I want to be the dragon in the play. Say it with me. I want to be the dragon in the play. Excellent! But Birimo wants to be the dragon, too. What can they do? Let's read the list of roles. "The Princess and the Dragon. Roles: the princess, brave and kind. The dragon, big and loud. The knight, strong and helpful. The little bird, small and clever. Do you want a role? Come to the audition tomorrow at ten o'clock. From Mr. Hoot." How many roles are there? Four. When is the audition? Tomorrow at ten. Now, phonics. Oh no! The dragon is coming! High and surprised. Oh no… I forgot my lines. Low and sad. I'm so happy! High and bright. I'm so sleepy… Low and slow. Your voice tells the feeling. Which role do you want? Think about it!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I want to be the dragon in the play. Today is audition day! Everyone shows what they can do. Mr. Hoot and I sit at a long table. When it's your turn, say what you are good at. After good at, we use an ing word, just like after enjoy. I'm good at singing. Can I try? Say it with me. I'm good at singing. Can I try? Very good! Haru and Birimo both want to be the dragon. Haru roars. Birimo roars, too. Whose roar is bigger? Let's read Mr. Hoot's audition notes. "Audition notes. Riko is good at speaking clearly. She can be the princess. Haru is good at sword fighting. Kiko is good at moving quickly, like a bird. Birimo is not good at dancing, but he is very good at roaring. What a roar!" What is Riko good at? Speaking clearly. What is Birimo good at? Roaring. Now, phonics. I did it! High and proud. I can't wait! High and excited. I can't do it… Low and worried. It's raining again… Low and sad. Next, please. It's your turn!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'm good at singing. Can I try? Today, Mr. Hoot puts the cast list on the wall. A cast list tells us who plays each role. To talk about it, we say, Riko plays the princess. Birimo plays the dragon. Say it with me. Riko plays the princess. Birimo plays the dragon. Perfect! Haru wanted to be the dragon. Is he sad? Let's read the cast list. "The Princess and the Dragon. Cast list. The princess: Riko. The dragon: Birimo, for his amazing roar. The knight: Haru, for his brave sword fighting. The little bird: Kiko. Director: Mr. Hoot, with help from Ms. Emma. First practice: tomorrow morning. Congratulations, everyone!" Who plays the knight? Haru does. Who helps Mr. Hoot? Ms. Emma does. Haru says, A knight is cool, too! Now, phonics. Let's review our feeling voices. Really?! High and surprised. Oh, really… Low and sad. I can't wait! High and excited. Oh no… I forgot my lines. Low and quiet. Great job! Congratulations to our new actors!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Riko plays the princess. Birimo plays the dragon. Today is our first practice. Riko holds the script. Her hands are shaking. She says, I'm nervous. Say it with me. I'm nervous. Good! When a friend is nervous, we can help. We say, Don't worry. You'll be great. Let's say that, too. Don't worry. You'll be great. Being nervous is normal. Even famous actors feel nervous. Let's read a note from Mr. Hoot. "Tips for nervous actors. First, take a deep breath. Second, shake your hands and smile. Third, look at a friend in the audience. Remember, everyone makes mistakes at practice. Practice is the place for mistakes. Have fun and do your best!" What is the first tip? Take a deep breath. Where can you make mistakes? At practice. Now, phonics. Today we have words with ed and ing. Tired. I feel tired. Tiring. The practice is tiring. Relaxed. I feel relaxed. Relaxing. A warm bath is relaxing. Ed is how you feel. Ing is what makes you feel it. Take a deep breath, and let's start!

phonics.tipJa: I'm excited!（わたしは わくわく して いる）と The play is exciting.（げきが わくわくさせる）。excite の e を とって excited・exciting。interest は そのまま interested・interesting。

おもしろい・きょうみぶかい

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'm nervous. Today, we read the exciting part of the play. Listen to two words. Excited. Exciting. They look the same, but they are different. Excited（わくわく） is how a person feels. Exciting is about the thing. It makes you feel that way. The play is exciting. I'm excited! Say it with me. The play is exciting. I'm excited! Wonderful! We can't say, I'm exciting, when we mean our feeling. Let's read a page from Mr. Hoot's play. "The princess walks into the dark forest. Suddenly, she hears a big roar. A dragon flies over the trees! The princess is surprised, but she is not afraid. The knight runs to her side. The little bird sings a warning song. Everyone in the audience holds their breath." Is this part exciting? Yes, it is! How does the audience feel? Excited! Now, phonics. Excited. I'm excited. Exciting. The play is exciting. Interested. I'm interested in dragons. Interesting. This story is interesting. Ed for people's feelings. Ing for things. Let's turn the page!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, The play is exciting. I'm excited! Today, we practice scene three. In this scene, the king talks for a long, long time. Birimo is yawning. Kiko is looking at the ceiling. Haru says, This scene is boring. Let's make it better. Say it with me. This scene is boring. Let's make it better. Great! Remember, boring is for the scene, and bored is for people. The scene is boring, so we are bored. How can we make it better? We can say, How about adding a song? Let's read the king's long speech. "Hello, my people. Today I will talk about the weather. Yesterday it was sunny. The day before, it was sunny, too. Last week, it was cloudy on Monday and sunny on Tuesday. Now, let me tell you about the clouds." Is it exciting? No, it's boring! What can we add? A song, a dance, or a joke. Now, phonics. Bored. I'm bored. Boring. The speech is boring. Amazed. The audience is amazed. Amazing. Your idea is amazing. Let's make this scene amazing!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, This scene is boring. Let's make it better. Today, we finished our first full practice! Now we sit in a circle and talk about our feelings. I ask, How do you feel now? Riko was nervous at first, but she remembered all her lines. She says, I feel proud of myself. Say it with me. I feel proud of myself. Beautiful! When you work hard, you can feel proud of yourself. Let's read Riko's practice diary. "Today was our first full practice. In the morning, I was worried. My hands were shaking. But Kiko said, 'You'll be great.' I took a deep breath and said my lines. I didn't forget anything! Birimo's roar was surprising and funny. Now I feel proud of myself." How did Riko feel in the morning? Worried. How does she feel now? Proud. Now, phonics. Surprised. I was surprised. Surprising. The roar was surprising. Worried. Change y to i, and add ed. Worrying. Keep the y, and add ing. Remember, feelings change. How do you feel now?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I feel proud of myself. Today, we play a game called Feelings Charades. One actor shows a feeling with their face and body, but says nothing. The others guess. You can ask, Are you surprised? Say it with me. Are you surprised? Good! If the guess is wrong, the actor says, No, I'm confused! Let's say that, too. No, I'm confused! Actors use their faces and bodies to show feelings, so this game is great practice. Let's read the game rules from Mr. Hoot. "Feelings Charades. One player picks a feeling card. Don't show it to anyone! Show the feeling with your face, hands, and body. No words, please. The other players ask questions, like 'Are you nervous?' The first correct guess wins a point. Then it's the next player's turn." Can you use words? No! What do the other players do? They ask questions. Now, phonics. Let's review. Confused. I'm confused. Confusing. This map is confusing. Exciting. The game is exciting. I'm so happy! High and bright. Okay, pick a card!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we played a feelings game. Are you surprised? No, I'm confused! Today, we have a problem. Mr. Hoot opened the old script, and the last pages are missing. Nobody knows the ending! So, what did the friends do? They made a big choice. We say, We decided to write our own play. Say it with me. We decided to write our own play. Great! Decided to means we chose to do it. Let's read Mr. Hoot's note. "Dear actors, I am so sorry. The last pages of The Princess and the Dragon are gone. Maybe the mice ate them. Please write a new story with your own ideas. A good story needs a hero, a problem, and a happy ending. I believe in you. Mr. Hoot." What does a good story need? A hero, a problem, and a happy ending. Who believes in the actors? Mr. Hoot does. Now, phonics. Today, we look at how we write lines. Let's write a play, said Riko. The comma goes inside the quotation marks. I'll be the narrator, said Haru. Kiko said, I have an idea. Good idea, said Ms. Emma. Now, let's write our own play!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, We decided to write our own play. Today, we think about the problem in our story. Every good story has a surprise. Something happens, and nobody expects it. We start with one word. Suddenly. Say it with me. Suddenly, the lights went out. Great! Can you feel the surprise? Let's read the first page of our new script. "The Princess and the Locked Tower. Long ago, a dragon took the town's music box. Now the town is quiet. Nobody sings, and nobody dances. The princess and the knight climb the tall tower to get it back. They walk up one hundred stairs. Suddenly, the lights go out. The tower is dark." Why is the town quiet? Because the dragon took the music box. Where do the princess and the knight go? They climb the tall tower. Now, phonics. Look at these lines. Help, shouted the princess. The exclamation mark goes inside the quotation marks. Run, cried the knight. Who's there, asked the dragon. The question mark goes inside, too. Look out, yelled the little bird. Now, what happened next? Let's think together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Suddenly, the lights went out. Oh no! The princess and the knight are in the dark tower. Now our story needs help. Something good happens. We start with another word. Luckily. Say it with me. Luckily, a little bird helped them. Wonderful! Suddenly brings a problem, and luckily brings help. Kiko plays the little bird. Let's read the next page of our script. "The tower is dark and cold. The princess whispers, 'I'm... I'm scared.' Then they hear a soft sound. Tweet, tweet! Luckily, a little bird flies in through the window. It finds a shiny key on the floor and brings a small light. Now the princess and the knight can see the stairs." What did the bird find? A shiny key. What did it bring? A small light. Now, phonics. Look at the three dots. They show a pause. I'm, I'm scared, whispered the princess. Wait, what's that sound, asked the knight. The door is, locked, said the bird. Stop a little at the dots. Luckily, I have a key, said the bird. Let's read our lines with little pauses!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Luckily, a little bird helped them. Today, we write the most exciting part of the story. The princess and the knight want to run away from the dark tower. They try, but there is a problem. We say, They tried to escape, but the door was locked. Say it with me. They tried to escape, but the door was locked. Excellent! Tried to means they did their best, but it didn't work. Let's read the big scene. "The princess and the knight run down the stairs. They try to open the big gate, but it is locked. Then the little bird gives them the key. Click! The gate opens. 'We're free!' they shout. But the dragon flies down. 'Please stay,' he says in a small voice. 'I took the music box because I was lonely.'" Why did the dragon take the music box? Because he was lonely. What did he say? Please stay. Now, phonics. We're free, shouted the friends. Is anyone there, called the princess. Oh, thank you, said the dragon, with a little pause after oh. The dragon said, Please stay. The comma comes before the quotation marks. What a scene!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, They tried to escape, but the door was locked. Now our story is ready. Today, we show the whole story to Mr. Hoot. A good story has four parts. Say it with me. Our story has a beginning, a problem, a solution, and an ending. Great! Let's read our story outline on the big board. "Beginning: A lonely dragon takes the town's music box. The princess and the knight climb the tower. Problem: Suddenly, the lights go out, and the gate is locked. Solution: Luckily, a little bird finds the key and brings a light. Ending: The dragon says sorry, and they all play music together." What is the problem? The lights go out, and the gate is locked. What is the solution? A little bird finds the key. And the ending? They play music together. Now, phonics. Let's look back. Help, shouted the princess. The exclamation mark goes inside. Let's write a play, said Riko. The comma goes inside, too. The door is, locked, said the bird. Pause at the dots. And amazing. Amaze, amazing. Mr. Hoot says our story is amazing!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Our story has a beginning, a problem, a solution, and an ending. Now it's time to practice our lines. Mr. Hoot says, Words are not enough. Say it with feeling. Say it with me. Say it with feeling. Great! When the gate opens, the princess says, I'm free! Is she happy or sad? She's very happy! So she says it with a big, bright voice. Let's read Mr. Hoot's acting tips. "Acting Tips from Mr. Hoot. One: Think about the feeling first. Is your character happy, sad, angry, or surprised? Two: Use your face and your body, too. Three: Change your voice. Happy lines are high and bright. Sad lines are low and slow. Four: Listen to the echoes. They love real feelings!" What should you think about first? The feeling. How are sad lines? Low and slow. Now, phonics. Which word is strong? I want the RED cape. Not the blue one! The show starts at SIX. Not five! Can you OPEN the door? Not close it! We need TWO chairs. Not three! Now, say your lines with feeling!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Say it with feeling. Today, Mr. Hoot sits at the very back of the theater. He listens to Riko's lines, but he can't hear her well. Her voice is too small. So, what does he say? Speak louder, please. The people at the back can't hear. Say it with me. Speak louder, please. The people at the back can't hear. Good job! And if someone talks too fast, we say, Speak more slowly. Let's read the sign next to the stage. "Voice Practice. Stand up tall and breathe in deeply. Speak from your stomach, not your throat. Look at the people at the back and send your voice to them. Don't hurry. Slow and clear is better than fast and quiet. Big voice, big feelings!" Where should you look? At the people at the back. Which is better, fast and quiet or slow and clear? Slow and clear. Now, phonics. SHE plays the princess. She, not someone else! RIKO sang this song. Riko, not Haru. This is MY line. Mine, not yours! We practice on MONDAY. Monday, not Tuesday. Now, big voices, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Speak louder, please. The people at the back can't hear. Today, something funny happened backstage. Ms. Emma's cake was on the table. Now it's gone, and Birimo has cream on his face! Birimo says, I didn't eat YOUR cake. Listen. Your is strong. So what does he mean? He ate a different cake! Say it with me. I didn't eat YOUR cake. Great! One sentence can mean different things. It depends on the strong word. Let's read the note on the table. "Backstage Snack Table. Two cakes are here today. The big chocolate cake is for Ms. Emma. The small strawberry cake is for Birimo. Please eat only your own cake. And please share the cookies. There are six cookies for the whole team. Thank you! Mr. Hoot." Whose cake is the strawberry one? Birimo's. How many cookies are there? Six. Now, phonics. I didn't eat YOUR cake. Strong on your. I didn't say SHE took it. Strong on she. Birimo ate the LAST cookie. The last one! My BROTHER made this crown. Brother, not sister. Which word is important? You decide!

phonics.tipJa: The bird FOUND the key.（なくしたのでは なく みつけた）・I'll bring the props TOMORROW.（あした）・Haru was the KNIGHT.（きしの やく）・I like your BLUE hat.（あおい ぼうし）。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I didn't eat YOUR cake. Today, we read something special in our script. Some words are not for saying. They tell actors how to move. We call them stage directions. Here is one. Walk to the center. Then, look up. Say it with me. Walk to the center. Then, look up. Good! We also say enter for coming onto the stage and exit for leaving. Let's read a page with stage directions. They are in brackets. "Scene Three. The top of the tower. (The knight enters from the left. He walks to the center. Then, he looks up.) Knight: 'The dragon must be up there.' (The little bird flies in from the right. It drops a key.) Knight: 'Thank you, little bird!' (The knight picks up the key and exits to the right.)" Where does the knight enter from? The left. What does the bird drop? A key. Now, phonics. The bird FOUND the key. Found, not lost! I'll bring the props TOMORROW. Tomorrow, not today. Haru was the KNIGHT. The knight, not the dragon. I like your BLUE hat. Blue, not red. Let's follow the stage directions!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Walk to the center. Then, look up. Today, we practice our play scene by scene. We use everything. Feelings, big voices, strong words, and stage directions. Let's start with the last scene. The dragon is alone in the tower. Someone knocks on the door. The dragon asks, Who's there? Say it with me. Who's there? Good! Then the princess answers, It's me, your friend! When a scene doesn't go well, we say, Let's try that scene again. From the top! Let's read the last scene. "Scene Five. (The dragon sits alone. Knock, knock.) Dragon: 'Who's there?' Princess: 'It's me, your friend! We brought the music box back. Let's play it together.' Dragon: 'Oh... thank you.' (Everyone sings. The town is happy again.)" Who knocks on the door? The princess. What do they do together? They sing and play music. Now, phonics. I didn't eat YOUR cake. Strong on your. The show starts at SIX. Strong on six. Who's there, asked the dragon. The question mark goes inside. Oh, thank you, said the dragon. Pause after oh. Let's try that scene again. From the top!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Who's there? It's me, your friend! Today, we're making costumes and props for our play. A princess needs a crown. A knight needs a cape. So we say, We need a crown and a cape. Say it with me. We need a crown and a cape. Great! And guess what? A letter came from the Cave of Riddles. Cora the crow carried it here. Let's read it. "Dear friends, I heard about your play. Please use my crystal crown on the stage. Cora is bringing it to you. She wants to say thank you and sorry again. Take good care of it, and have a wonderful show! Your friend, Luma." Who sent the crown? Luma did. Who is bringing it? Cora the crow is. How kind! We still need a cape, a sword and a music box. Kiko is good at sewing, so she'll make the cape. To ask for more ideas, say, What else do we need? Now, phonics. Tongue twisters help us speak clearly. Crazy crows carry crunchy crackers. Slowly first. Now faster! A creaky crown and a crumpled cape. Pink paper props pop on the purple stage. Pip packs puppets in purple paper. Lips together, pop! Let's get making!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, We need a crown and a cape. Now we have them all. Today is the dress rehearsal. A dress rehearsal is the last practice before the show. We wear our costumes and act the whole play, from the beginning to the end. It feels different in costumes! So we say, It's fun to act in costumes! Say it with me. It's fun to act in costumes! Wonderful! Let's read Mr. Hoot's rehearsal plan. "Dress rehearsal plan: Four o'clock, put on your costumes. Four fifteen, check the lights and the music. Four thirty, start from the top. Do not stop, even if you make a mistake. Keep going! After that, we will talk about the good points." What time do we start the play? At four thirty. What should you do after a mistake? Keep going! Birimo's dragon wings are very big, so it's hard to walk through the door. Take small steps, Birimo! Now, phonics. Three thin thumbs and thirty thick threads. Tongue between your teeth. Think first, then thank the theater. Cheerful children choose cheese and cherries. A chubby chick chews chocolate chips. Ch, ch, ch! Places, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It's fun to act in costumes! Today is the big day. The show starts in ten minutes. Everyone is a little nervous. Before a show, actors say a funny thing to each other. Break a leg!（がんばって） It doesn't mean, Hurt your leg. It means, Good luck! Have a great show! Say it with me. Break a leg! And the answer is, Thanks! I'll do my best. Let's read a card from Mr. Hoot. "To my brave new actors. Your hearts may be beating fast. That's OK. It means you care about the show. Take a deep breath. Look at your friends and smile. Remember, the echoes are waiting for your voices. Break a leg, everyone! Mr. Hoot." Why are your hearts beating fast? Because you care about the show. What should you do? Take a deep breath. If a friend's hands are shaking, say, You can do it! Now, phonics. Let's warm up our tongues. Riko rolls a round red rug. Tongue back, no touching. Lucky Lulu lights little lamps. Tongue up behind your teeth. Real rabbits run around the rocks. Lily's lion loves lemon lollipops. R and L, great! Now, break a leg!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Break a leg! Thanks! I'll do my best. And now, it's showtime! The curtain is going up. Today, we tell the story of our play, so we use the past. The princess opened the gate. Say it with me. The princess opened the gate. Great! Let's read the story page from the program. "The Princess and the Locked Tower. One day, a princess and a knight climbed a tall tower. They wanted to get back the town's music box. Suddenly, the lights went out. The door was locked! Luckily, a little bird found the key. The princess opened the gate. The lonely dragon said, 'Please stay.' In the end, they all played music together." Who found the key? The little bird did. Why did the dragon take the music box? Because he was lonely. And listen! When Riko shouted, I'm free, the theater answered, free, free, free! The echoes are coming back! Now, phonics. Brave Birimo bakes big blue buns. Lips together for b. Very vivid violets in a velvet vase. Teeth on your lip for v. Five funny frogs find a flute. Fresh fruit for four friends. Quiet air for f. What a show!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, The princess opened the gate. The show is over, and the audience is clapping. Now it's time to say nice things to each other. You were amazing! I loved the ending. Say it with me. You were amazing! I loved the ending. Wonderful! When a friend says something nice to you, say, Thank you! You were great, too. Let's read the notes from the audience. "Thank you for the wonderful play! The dark scene was exciting. The little bird was so brave. I laughed when the dragon cried, 'Please stay.' The music at the end was beautiful. I loved the ending! From Lulu, Mr. Hoot and the echoes." Which scene was exciting? The dark scene. How was the music at the end? Beautiful. Here's a tip. Be specific. Don't only say, Good job. Say what you liked. My favorite part was the dark scene. Now, phonics. Let's review. Crazy crows carry crunchy crackers. Five funny frogs find a flute. I didn't say SHE took it. Strong on she. We need TWO chairs. Strong on two. You were all amazing!

And what can we do better next time? The best part was the dragon's song. Say it with me. The best part was the dragon's song. Next time, we should speak more slowly. Great! Let's read Mr. Hoot's notes. "Notes on the play: The best part was the dragon's song. Everyone was quiet and listened. The lights and the music were perfect. But some lines were too fast. Next time, we should speak more slowly and look at the audience. I am proud of you all!" What was the best part? The dragon's song. What should we do next time? lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, The best part was the dragon's song. Next time, we should speak more slowly. Today, you're the writer! We'll write a short script. In a script, the narrator tells the story, and the characters say their lines. Narrator: One day, a fox found a magic hat. Say it with me. Narrator: One day, a fox found a magic hat. Good! Let's read Kiko's short script. "Narrator: One day, a fox found a magic hat. Fox: 'Look at my new hat!' Narrator: Suddenly, the hat began to sing. Rabbit: 'Wow! A singing hat!' Fox: 'Let's sing together!' Narrator: In the end, they sang all night under the moon." What did the fox find? A magic hat. What happened suddenly? The hat began to sing. In a script, write the name, then a colon, then the line. Eight to ten lines is perfect. Now, phonics. Kiko said, I have an idea. The comma comes before the quotation marks. Interesting. Something interesting. I can't wait! High and excited. This is MY line. Strong on my. Pink paper props pop on the purple stage. Pop your lips! Now, write your own script!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Narrator: One day, a fox found a magic hat. Today, we'll play Story Circle. We sit in a circle. Each person says only one word. Together, we make a story. Let's make a story one word at a time. Say it with me. Let's make a story one word at a time. Great! Here are the rules. Let's read them. "Story Circle rules: Sit in a circle with three friends. Say one word, then point to the next person. Listen carefully to every word. Don't stop the story. If the story gets silly, that's OK. Laugh and keep going! At the end, say the whole story together." How many words do you say? Only one. What if the story gets silly? Laugh and keep going! Let's start. Once. Upon. A. Time. When it's your friend's turn, say, It's your turn! Now, phonics. Well, okay… Low and quiet. Bored. A person feels bored. Wait, what's that sound, asked the knight. The three dots mean a little pause. The bird FOUND the key. Strong on found. Three thin thumbs and thirty thick threads. Tongue between your teeth. Your turn!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Let's make a story one word at a time. Today is our goodbye show at the Theater of Echoes. Let's remember everything. First, we talked about what we enjoy. I enjoy singing on the stage. Say it with me. I enjoy singing on the stage. We also talked about our choices. I decided to try something new. Great! Let's read Mr. Hoot's goodbye letter. "Dear friends, thank you for bringing the echoes back. My theater is full of voices again. Tomorrow, take the mountain road to the east. You will find the Village of Springs. The spring water there is warm. Rest your tired feet. Please come back and act again someday! Mr. Hoot." Where does the mountain road go? To the Village of Springs. How is the water there? Warm. Now, phonics. Thank you so much! High and happy. Amazing. Something amazing. We're free, shouted the friends. The exclamation mark goes inside the quotation marks. Haru was the KNIGHT. Strong on knight. Lucky Lulu lights little lamps. Tongue up for l. Let's start our goodbye show!

segments.subtitleJa: からだを うごかそう！ スピード ことば！ みて！ とまって！ こっちへ きて！ いって！
segments.subtitleEn: Let's move! Speed words! Look! Stop! Come here! Go!

segments.say: Bow to the audience. Now cup your ears and listen to the echoes. Can you hear them?
segments.subtitleJa: おきゃくさんに おじぎ して。こんどは みみに てを あてて、こだまを きいて。きこえる？
segments.subtitleEn: Bow to the audience. Now cup your ears and listen to the echoes. Can you hear them?

slide.title: Let's move!
items: Cup your ears and listen to the echoes.

segments.say: Clap for everyone! Last challenge! Go! Bow! Listen! Clap!
segments.subtitleJa: みんなに はくしゅ！ さいごの チャレンジ！ いって！ おじぎ！ きいて！ はくしゅ！
segments.subtitleEn: Clap for everyone! Last challenge! Go! Bow! Listen! Clap!

slide.title: Let's move!
items: Cup your ears and listen to the echoes.

segments.say: Repeat after me. Thank you for watching our play!
segments.subtitleJa: まねして いってね。「わたしたちの げきを みて くれて ありがとう！」
segments.subtitleEn: Repeat after me. Thank you for watching our play!

slide.title: Say it!
items: Thank you for watching our play!

segments.say: We hope you enjoyed it.
segments.subtitleJa: 「たのしんで もらえたら うれしいです。」
segments.subtitleEn: We hope you enjoyed it.

segments.say: Did you have fun? Yes! It was the best show ever!
segments.subtitleJa: 「たのしかった？ うん！ いままでで いちばんの ショー だった！」
segments.subtitleEn: Did you have fun? Yes! It was the best show ever!

slide.title: Say it!
items: Did you have fun? ― Yes! It was the best show ever!

segments.say: Your turn! Your family came to see your dance. Thank them. Thank you for watching my dance!
segments.subtitleJa: あなたの ばん！ おうちの ひとが あなたの ダンスを みに きたよ。おれいを いって。「わたしの ダンスを みて くれて ありがとう！」
segments.subtitleEn: Your turn! Your family came to see your dance. Thank them. Thank you for watching my dance!

slide.title: Say it!
items: Thank you for watching our play!

segments.say: Quiz time! The show is over. What do you say to the audience? A, Thank you for watching our play! B, Break a leg! Think!
segments.subtitleJa: クイズ！ ショーが おわったよ。おきゃくさんに なんて いう？ A、Thank you for watching our play! B、Break a leg! かんがえて！
segments.subtitleEn: Quiz time! The show is over. What do you say to the audience? A, Thank you for watching our play! B, Break a leg! Think!

slide.title: Quiz
items: Thank you for watching our play!

segments.say: It's A! Break a leg is before the show. After the show, say thank you. Bravo!
segments.subtitleJa: こたえは A！ Break a leg は ショーの まえ。ショーの あとは ありがとうと いおう。ブラボー！
segments.subtitleEn: It's A! Break a leg is before the show. After the show, say thank you. Bravo!

slide.title: Answer
items: Thank you for watching our play!

segments.say: You did it! You can thank an audience. You can talk with feeling, and the echoes came back! Next, go and talk with Birimo! Next is World 27, the Village of Springs! Bye-bye!
segments.subtitleJa: やったね！ おきゃくさんに おれいが いえるね。きもちを こめて はなせて、こだまも もどって きた！ このあと ビリモと おはなし してね！ つぎは ワールド27、いずみの さと！ バイバイ！
segments.subtitleEn: You did it! You can thank an audience. You can talk with feeling, and the echoes came back! Next, go and talk with Birimo! Next is World 27, the Village of Springs! Bye-bye!

slide.title: Today's wrap-up
items: Thank you for watching our play!
Did you have fun? ― Yes! It was the best show ever!
